title: An Experiential Approach to AI Literacy
extended_summary:
This position paper addresses a practical gap in AI literacy: people may hear about AI and understand it in the abstract, yet still struggle to identify where AI fits into their real workflows or how to judge whether it is appropriate for a given task. The authors argue that AI education often creates “knowing” without “doing,” especially for non-technical audiences, and propose an approach that makes AI literacy more grounded, contextual, and useful.

The proposed intervention is an experiential AI literacy model with three phases. First, participants take part in an interactive workshop that introduces high-level concepts of AI, including how it works, what it can and cannot do, and how to evaluate its use. Second, over roughly 2–4 weeks, participants reflect on their daily work experiences and brainstorm potential AI use cases in their own contexts using design tools and short activities. Third, they return for a sharing workshop where they present and refine these use cases through storytelling, including discussion of opportunities, limitations, fairness, privacy, accountability, and workflow integration.

The intended population is stakeholders in diverse workplaces, with examples including nurses in emergency departments, elementary school teachers, and municipal government workers. The paper is not an empirical evaluation; instead, it is a conceptual proposal grounded in prior AI literacy and experiential learning literature. The authors conclude that embedding AI literacy in participants’ own lived and work experiences should support deeper understanding, better participatory design of AI systems, and more practical, stakeholder-centered AI use-case development.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A generic generative AI/LLM chatbot or assistant used for broad AI capability discussion and ideation, without a specific commercial or research product being evaluated.
identified_tools.use_case: This position paper proposes an experiential AI literacy approach that references generic examples of AI such as chatbots, but does not empirically evaluate any specific AI tool in K-12 reading or literacy instruction.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a theoretical/position paper proposing an experiential AI literacy approach. It does not report an empirical study, comparison group, or outcome data relevant to K-12 reading or literacy.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct evidence is presented on learner outcomes, effect sizes, or impacts relative to business-as-usual or non-AI supports.
